economy.summary: His campaign site says he wants data centers to pay their fair share in utilities rather than passing costs on to residents, citing rising electric bills, and says he will work on a program to incentivize landlords to lower rent.
economy.short: Wants data centers paying utility costs; proposes incentives lowering rents.

taxes.summary: His campaign site says property tax should not be a barrier to owning a home; he proposes expanding the Homestead Exemption and decreasing the tax burden on homeowners.
taxes.short: Proposes expanding Homestead Exemption, decreasing homeowner property-tax burden.

education.summary: His campaign site calls recent cyber charter school reforms a first step and says he wants to close loopholes, hold cyber charter schools to the same standards as brick-and-mortar schools, and make sure local schools are not going bankrupt.
education.short: Supports further cyber charter reform; same standards as brick-and-mortar.

energy.summary: His campaign site says he supports the three-year moratorium on data centers and will continue working to hold data centers accountable, drawing on his 15 years in the technology industry.
energy.short: Supports three-year data center moratorium; wants centers held accountable.

economy.summary: His campaign site says he supports small business growth and shopping locally over big box stores, and opposes expanding government control that he says burdens businesses. In a 2024 WVIA interview he opposed minimum wage increases, saying government should stay out of small business.
economy.short: Supports small businesses; opposes government burdens and minimum-wage increases.

taxes.summary: In a 2024 WVIA candidate interview he favored lowering or eliminating property taxes with some combination of higher sales or income taxes; his campaign site also opposes the stormwater fee he calls a rain tax and supports reducing government size and spending.
taxes.short: Favors lowering property taxes via higher sales or income taxes.

abortion.summary: In a 2024 WVIA candidate interview he said life begins at conception and that he opposes abortion except when the mother's life is in jeopardy; he supports encouraging adoption in cases of rape and incest and supports legislation ensuring access to in vitro fertilization.
abortion.short: Opposes abortion except to save mother's life; supports IVF access.

education.summary: In a 2024 WVIA candidate interview he supported school vouchers so money follows the child to better-performing schools including private options, said the current funding system unfairly benefits Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, and opposed funding parity for cyber charter schools since they lack brick-and-mortar expenses.
education.short: Supports school vouchers; opposes cyber charter funding parity.

energy.summary: As the incumbent, in May 2026 he introduced companion bills that would pause data center applications so municipalities can update zoning ordinances, and would repeal the state's computer data center equipment tax exemption, redirecting the recovered revenue to reduce the gas tax.
energy.short: Introduced bills pausing data center applications, repealing their tax exemption.

guns.summary: In a 2024 WVIA candidate interview he opposed further gun regulation, saying existing systems already in place work fine; his campaign site says he supports Second Amendment rights for responsible gun owners.
guns.short: Opposes further gun regulation; supports Second Amendment rights.
